rv.q: What Zeller catches admirably is the way Andre, a retired engineer, still clings to an authority he is no longer capable of executing.
The Father ‘s a play you have to see to know yourself, and those you love, better.
It’s an uncomfortable performance, brilliant in its understanding and its detail.
The central contrivance is intellectually engaging yet at ninety minutes it leaves you plenty of time for dinner before the train back to the suburbs and contains nothing to put you off your food.

cn.t: Zeller's inventive Alzheimer's drama earns acclaim for its immersive perspective and Cranham's powerful performance, though some find it overpraised. The production's clever design effectively disorients audiences into experiencing dementia firsthand.
